solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stirred chaff up, like old liquor

indicators.note: something stirred is mixed about, so the following letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up chaff, in a scene that somehow resembles an old drink.
explanation.walkthrough: HUFFCAP is an archaic adjective for strong, heady ale that makes drinkers swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Huffcap was an old description of potent, heady beer, so it is an adjective characterising strong ale of former times.

clue.text: Cavalry essential? Armies short of tons

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the item named next is taken out of the word before

parts.note: a host is an army
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A military puzzle: what does cavalry need, if armies run short of tonnage?
explanation.walkthrough: HOSTS loses its T. HOSS is an American dialect spelling of horse, which is what any cavalry cannot do without.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavalry are mounted soldiers, so a horse is their indispensable requirement; the question mark flags the dialect spelling.

clue.text: Huge old fossil in Spanish country house, headless, look yonder

indicators.note: without a head means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a quinta is a country house or estate in Spain or Portugal
'there!' points at something over yonder

explanation.surface: A tourist spots a giant fossil at a Spanish villa and points it out.
explanation.walkthrough: The uintathere was a huge horned mammal of the Eocene, named after the Uinta Mountains of Utah.
explanation.definitionFit: The uintathere is an extinct, rhinoceros-sized mammal known only from fossil remains, hence a huge ancient creature.

clue.text: Uncle trained in further education displaying volubility

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: FE is the standard abbreviation for further education

indicators.note: trained suggests being put through a process and reshaped, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An uncle who went through a college course now talks fluently.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters sit between F and E. FLUENCE is an old word for fluency.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluence is an obsolete form of fluency, and volubility is a ready, flowing ease of speech.

clue.text: Forming packed mass about royal on board?

parts.note: ca is the abbreviation of circa, about
the king is a royal piece on a chessboard

explanation.surface: Something clumps together around a royal visitor aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship; the question mark points instead to a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Caking is the process of a substance clotting or hardening into a solid cake-like lump.

clue.text: Gay plan formed with hearts — it consists of two prints

indicators.note: formed means shaped into something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A cheerful scheme drawn up with love produces a picture of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: An ANAGLYPH is a stereoscopic picture made of two superimposed images in different colours, seen in 3D through coloured glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereoscopic anaglyph superimposes two slightly offset coloured images, so it is literally made from a pair of prints.

clue.text: Affliction of starving kids — lack of parent

parts.note: no means none, an absence
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Hungry children suffer, made worse by having no parent to care for them.
explanation.walkthrough: NOMA is a gangrenous ulceration of the mouth and face that strikes malnourished children.
explanation.definitionFit: Noma is a destructive gangrene affecting severely undernourished youngsters, so it is a disease of hungry children.

clue.text: A lean-to with five columns in front, a style disregarded

indicators.note: what is disregarded is ignored and dropped, so those letters are left out

parts.note: a pentastyle portico has five columns across its front
taken as written

explanation.surface: An architect describes a modest shed with a five-columned frontage, ignoring fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing A STYLE from the end of PENTASTYLE leaves PENT, short for penthouse in its old sense of a sloping lean-to.
explanation.definitionFit: A pent, or penthouse, is a shed with a single sloping roof built against a wall, exactly what a lean-to is.

clue.text: Mulled wines scald with matches

parts.note: plot is a Scots verb meaning to scald
ties are sporting fixtures, matches

explanation.surface: Hot spiced wine burns someone's mouth at a sports fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: PLOTTIES is a Scots word for hot spiced drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotty is a Scottish term for a hot drink of wine with spices, so the plural names several heated, spiced wines.

clue.text: Old magistrate to cut off, rising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to elide is to omit or cut off a sound

explanation.surface: An ancient official was removed from office and then rose again.
explanation.walkthrough: EDILE is a variant spelling of aedile, a Roman magistrate in charge of public buildings and games.
explanation.definitionFit: Aediles were officials of ancient Rome who supervised buildings, markets and festivals; edile is an alternative spelling.

clue.text: Quivering, having drunk Merlot with duck

indicators.note: a drunk is unsteady and confused, so the wine's letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone is shaking after downing red wine with their roast duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as swallowed with the wine as its object; it is the signal to jumble. TREMOLO is a musical trembling effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremolo is a rapid wavering in pitch or volume of a note, a trembling or shaking in music.

clue.text: Place for milkmaid with husband, not so recent — one holds security

parts.note: in Scots a loan is an open space where cows are milked
H is the abbreviation for husband
older is less new

explanation.surface: A rural scene: a dairymaid's milking yard, an ageing husband, and a man holding collateral.
explanation.walkthrough: LOAN (or loaning) is a Scots dialect word for a lane or milking place.
explanation.definitionFit: A loanholder is a creditor or mortgagee who holds a pledge or charge as security for money lent.

clue.text: Number in drain was cringing

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the word that follows

parts.note: to suck dry is to drain
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Someone figuring in a drain was cowering there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure, and 'was cringing' a description of it; N goes inside SUCK. SNUCK is the informal past tense of sneak, which can mean to behave meanly or cringingly.
explanation.definitionFit: To sneak can mean to act in a mean, cringing, servile way, and snuck is its colloquial past tense.

clue.text: Branch I got in tangle making large wardrobe

parts.note: an arm is a branch, as of a river or organisation

indicators.note: what has got in is now inside, so the pronoun is placed within the following word

parts.note: ore is a name for tangle, the oarweed seaweed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree branch I caught in a snarl ends up making a big cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tangle' looks like a muddle and invites an anagram; it is the seaweed tangle, also called oarweed.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoire is a tall, often ornate, free-standing cupboard for clothes, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Earn renewed activity around century, being born anew

indicators.note: renewed means made over again, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: around has the word for activity enclose the abbreviation

parts.note: the scene is where the action is, a sphere of activity
C is the abbreviation for century

explanation.surface: Renewed earnings over a hundred years bring a sort of rebirth.
explanation.walkthrough: The century letter goes inside the activity word just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascence is a rebirth or revival, the state of coming into existence a second time.

clue.text: Stalk to check, one circling equipment

indicators.note: circling goes round, so the word for checking surrounds the word for equipment

parts.note: to stem is to check or stop a flow
a rig is a set of equipment
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone stalks off to inspect, while another walks round the kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalk' tempts as a verb; it is the botanical noun. A sterigma is a tiny stalk bearing a spore in fungi.
explanation.definitionFit: In mycology a sterigma is a small slender projection supporting a spore, so it is a minute stalk.

clue.text: The old proceed, fluttered by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is judged on how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: fanned means waved or fluttered

explanation.surface: An elderly person moves on, flapping about, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: FAND is an obsolete word meaning to try or set out on an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Fand is archaic English for attempting or going forward with something, so it stands for an old way of proceeding.

clue.text: Font, sort of barrel with tarnished blue within

indicators.note: within places the jumbled letters inside the barrel word

parts.note: a drum is a cylindrical container, a type of barrel

indicators.note: something tarnished is spoilt, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A typeface described as a barrel shape with dull blue inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Font' looks like typography; here it is a basin for holy water. DELUBRUM is a Latin word for a shrine or a font.
explanation.definitionFit: A delubrum is a temple or shrine, and in church use a font or water basin for baptism.

clue.text: Soak in foreign river and atmosphere climbing in SA city

indicators.note: in puts the word for soaking inside the river name

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
to ret is to soak flax

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means the word reads upwards, back to front

parts.note: air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A traveller bathes abroad, then climbs into the air, ending up in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: To ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it; the Po is the foreign river, in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is the administrative capital of South Africa, so it is a South African city.

clue.text: Secretary reproduced notes

indicators.note: reproduced suggests copied in a new form, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An office secretary types up the notes taken in a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Steno is short for stenographer, a shorthand typist working as a secretary.

clue.text: Comment in school — owlish observation?

indicators.note: in places the remark inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
a crit is a critique, a critical comment

explanation.surface: A teacher's remark at school is a wise owl's observation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Owlish' suggests wise; it means literally from an owl. SCRITCH is a screech, the cry of an owl.
explanation.definitionFit: A scritch is a shrill screech, the call a screech owl makes, humorously treated as an owl's remark.

clue.text: Spun gold, airy and spiral

indicators.note: spun means whirled around, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Delicate gold thread is spun into an airy coil.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyroidal describes an arrangement whose parts turn in a helix, so it means spiralling.

clue.text: Once almost got up in clothes displaying sobriety

indicators.note: in puts the reversed letters inside the clothing word

parts.note: dress is clothing

indicators.note: in a down entry got up means the old word reads upwards

parts.note: ny is an old spelling of nigh, almost; 'Once' marks it as obsolete

explanation.surface: Someone almost got dressed once, and showed they were sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once almost' reads as a single hesitation; 'Once' marks the next word as obsolete, and NY is an old spelling of nigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryness can mean abstinence from alcohol, the state of being teetotal, which is sobriety.

clue.text: Bit of crab? That was useful round island

indicators.note: a bit of the word is a single piece of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of crab

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the past-tense verb goes about the island abbreviation

parts.note: helped means was of use
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A piece of crab proved useful on an island trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of crab' serves twice: as the definition and as the source of C. I goes inside HELPED. A CHELIPED is the leg of a crab that carries a claw.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheliped is the pincer-bearing limb of a crustacean, literally a part of a crab's body.

clue.text: Fruit like this is bottled in what has little value

indicators.note: something bottled in is enclosed, so these words go inside the next word

parts.note: 'not worth a damn' means worthless
so means in this way

explanation.surface: A fruit preserved like this is bottled, though hardly worth anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottled' fits a picture of preserving fruit; it is the instruction to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small dark purple plum, a fruit.

clue.text: Problem to do with transport

parts.note: re means concerning
a bus is a form of transport

explanation.surface: A problem about getting around town.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a picture puzzle, an enigma in which images stand for words, so a problem to solve.

clue.text: Pour out Scotch, recipe in aid to digestion

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the digestive fluid word

parts.note: bile is a fluid that aids digestion
R stands for recipe, take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A doctor pours whisky as part of a remedy for indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky; it marks the answer as a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Birle is a Scots verb meaning to pour out drink or ply someone with liquor.

clue.text: Groom, bashful husband leaving church

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the abbreviation is taken out of the word before

parts.note: shy means bashful
H is the abbreviation for husband
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A shy bridegroom walks out of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' and 'husband' paint a wedding; the groom here works with horses. A SYCE is a groom in India.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a syce is a servant who looks after horses, a stable groom.

clue.text: Chemicals gypsy found in hop stems

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the first word goes within the second

parts.note: bines are the climbing stems of the hop
a Rom is a Romany man

explanation.surface: A traveller discovers chemicals hidden in the hop plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hop' looks like a jump; bines are the twining stems of the hop plant used in brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bromines refers to compounds of bromine, a reactive halogen element, so a set of chemicals.

clue.text: A crowd turning up in fenced enclosure

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means the words read upwards

parts.note: a mob is a crowd

explanation.surface: A crowd arrives inside a fenced paddock.
explanation.walkthrough: BOMA is an East African word for a stockaded enclosure for animals or a camp.
explanation.definitionFit: In East Africa a boma is a thorn or palisade stockade enclosing livestock or a settlement.

clue.text: What's in Jock's cellar? 50% sweet wine

indicators.note: fifty per cent means only half is kept and the rest discarded

parts.note: sauterne is a variant spelling of the sweet French white wine

explanation.surface: A Scot's cellar holds a sweet wine, half drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cellar' suggests a wine store, but the salt cellar is meant. SAUT is Scots for salt; Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt cellar holds salt, and saut is the Scots form of that word, so it fills a Scotsman's cellar.

clue.text: Distinctive character of wine I fed to rogue

indicators.note: something fed to another goes inside it

parts.note: a little terror is a rascal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wine's particular quality, given to a scoundrel to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside TERROR, before its final R.
explanation.definitionFit: Terroir is the combination of soil, climate and site that gives wine a unique flavour profile.

clue.text: Operatic episode presented by clubs in Indian army

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for the army

parts.note: sena is the Hindi word for an army
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A dramatic opera scene is staged by soldiers carrying clubs in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A scena is an elaborate dramatic solo scene in an opera, typically a recitative and aria.

clue.text: A cousin messed around chimney causing injury?

indicators.note: around has the jumbled letters enclose the chimney word
messed means muddled up, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
lum is Scots for a chimney

explanation.surface: A clumsy cousin fooling about with the chimney could hurt somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks injury in the sense of harm to a reputation rather than to the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumnious means slanderous, and slander is a wrong done to someone's good name, an injury in a figurative sense.

clue.text: Blood pigment creating energy in meat

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for meat

parts.note: ham is cured pork
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Red meat gets its iron content from a pigment in the blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Haem is the iron-containing component of haemoglobin, the red colouring of blood.

clue.text: Day in Athens, wandering remote

indicators.note: wandering means straying from a set path, so these letters drift into a new order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day
taken as written

explanation.surface: A day spent strolling around Athens, far from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remote' looks like an adjective for being far away; it is the noun, a remote control.
explanation.definitionFit: A handset can be a hand-held remote control used to operate a television or similar device.
